summary: SSE reconnect offset drift causes duplicated leading segments in resumed stream
description:
Issue summary: Customer NoteFlow Labs reports that when their client performs an SSE resume after a short network interruption, the resumed stream sometimes repeats the first ~1-3 sentence segments of the response (leading segments) before continuing. This appears correlated with multi-region failover and connection reuse across an edge proxy.

Impact: Repeated leading segments result in duplicated content visible to end-users and downstream parsers, causing confusion in generated notes and downstream deduplication to fail. Affects a handful of heavy streaming sessions (long-form generation) for a high-revenue customer on Dedicated capacity.

Environment: prod-us-west (dedicated pool), model redwood-open-7b-v2, client uses SSE-based streaming with resume tokens; traffic passes through our edge-proxy cluster behind a regional LB. Customer SDK version: noteflow-sdk-js@1.4.2.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long generation request (~2k+ tokens, multi-paragraph) from the NoteFlow web client using SSE streaming.
2) Midstream (~after first paragraph) simulate a short network blip (client disconnect / 3-6s).
3) Client reconnects using the SSE resume token via the same SDK flow and edge host; server accepts resume and resumes streaming.
4) Observe the first 1-3 sentence segments are replayed at the start of the resumed stream, then the stream proceeds (resulting in duplicated leading content).

Observed behavior: Duplicate leading segments appear in resumed SSE stream. Resume offset in server logs sometimes differs by +1 to +3 segments compared to the client's last-ack offset. Resume success is returned (HTTP 200) but the first resumed chunks include content already delivered prior to disconnect.

Expected behavior: Resume should pick up exactly after last delivered token/segment; no duplication or replays.

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- edge-proxy log (us-west-2-edge-03) around time of reconnect:
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.842Z] conn-id=abc123 resume-token=rt-9f2ff offset=114 client-ack=114
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.873Z] routed to streamer node=sr-22 resume-accepted offset=114 assigned-session=sess-81

- streamer runtime trace:
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.890Z] sess-81 last-emitted-seg=111 last-confirmed-offset=114 kv-cache-hit=true
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.901Z] resume-offset-translation=114 -> 111 (drift detected)
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.905Z] emitting segment 111 \"Summary: ...\" (again)

- client-SDK trace (customer):
  reconnect: resume-token=rt-9f2ff lastSeenSegment=114
  receive: seg 111,112,113,114,115... (first few chunks duplicated)

Attachments: customer exported session transcript and full developer console capture (uploaded to ticket).

Initial hypothesis: Offset mapping between resume tokens and runtime segment indices is drifting when sessions are handled by an edge proxy that performs short-lived connection handoffs. The edge sometimes routes the reconnect to a streamer that has a slightly different internal segment index base (off-by-N) because of ongoing prefix caching/partial flush between nodes. The runtime should reconcile resume-token -> absolute offset deterministically; current logic may use a best-effort translation that can produce small duplicates in high-throughput scenarios or during handoff.

investigation_notes:
Repro steps executed in staging: created two streamer nodes with independent prefix caches, simulated SSE disconnect and forced reconnect to alternate node. Confirmed scenario: resume-token contains a logical offset that requires per-node base translation when a node stores only a relative prefix length. If node A flushes to central storage and node B hasn't, node B applies stale base -> emits overlapping segments. Key observation: race window when prefix cache flushes and node evictions happen during handoff. Logs show consistent small positive drift (1-3 segments). Also noted some cases where client reported lastSeenSegment does not match server's last-confirmed-offset due to idempotent-ack aggregation on the edge.

Telemetry to add: record resume-token mapping latency, node-base-version per session, and count of resume-retries per session. Adding an alert to detect >0.5% resumed sessions with duplication.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: deployed edge-pinning patch (10s pin) to reduce cross-node resume during tight windows. Also increased prefix-cache flush frequency to reduce stale bases.

Long-term: runtime change to centralized resume-index lookup (consult central resume-index service for token->absolute offset) is in PR (runtime#2287) and will be staged next week. Also adding a verification step at resume: streamer will compare requested offset against last-emitted-seg range and, if mismatch <=3 segments, perform a fast-forward-skip for duplicates rather than re-emitting them.

Postmortem / Follow-ups: INT-4421 assigned to infra to review LB affinity settings; add an SLO for resumed-stream duplication rate. Ensure customer-facing SDK includes deduplication helpers and clear guidance on safe resume windows.
workaround: 1) Customers can increase client-side reconnect backoff to >10s to reduce probability of hitting cross-node handoff. 2) For Dedicated customers, ask Support to enable short-term edge-pinning (applied for NoteFlow Labs). 3) As a client workaround, detect duplicate leading segments by sequence id and drop them; SDK team will add helper method in next minor release.
final_status_update: 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation deployed to prod-us-west. Customer reported a significant reduction of duplicates during their validation window. Runtime centralized-lookup PR in review; plan rollout to prod-us-west in next week pending QA. Ticket remains In Progress until runtime change is fully deployed and customer confirms resolution for several production sessions.
